newsitem.title: UK: Brady market firm but quiet on U.S. holiday.
newsitem.headline: Brady market firm but quiet on U.S. holiday.

text.p: There was little trading of emerging market debt on Monday due to a U.S. holiday, although dealers said the sector had a firm tone.
"After last week's favourable (U.S. producer price index aUSPPI ) PPI figures the market is expecting very soft figures for Wednesday's (consumer price index) CPI," a debt trader at a U.S. bank said.
"There is definately a firm tone to the market. The feeling is the rally may not quite be over and there could be upside in a few more areas," he said.
Monday saw interest in Bulgaria and Russia in particular.
"There is a better bid in Bulgaria and Russia this morning," a debt trader at a European bank said. "(But) few trades have gone through, and it is generally very quiet."
Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR were bid at 58-3/4 cents in the dollar, up 2-1/4 points. FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR were up two points to 45-1/4 cents.

Prices on Bulgarian debt, the most volatile Brady sector, began to recover on Friday after its interim prime minister said talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on setting up a currency board would start this week.
Russian MinFin bonds were up slightly but Vneshekonombank dollar paper RUVNUSLNS=RR was marginally down. Latin American Brady debt was steady on Monday.
